review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its definitions are used downstream: TraceCocycle.lean (eval_wordExpr, eval_sumExpr, eval_delta_encoded, map_eval), MomentFlow.lean, UnitaryEvaluation.lean and FiniteMoments.lean. The file has no @[simp] lemmas and no simp attributes, so I judged it on the missing-interface criterion. Every client proof unfolds the definitions by name (`simp only [delta, eval, ...]`), which works because they are structurally recursive. The weakness is therefore moderate: there is no named simp set. I did not find a loop, competing rules or an unsuitable rewrite direction. I did not look at whether `norm_algebraMap'` is simp in the pinned Mathlib, and I made no claim about how the non-terminal `simp ...; ring` on line 140 behaves. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested.

findings.declaration: NCPolynomial.eval / NCPolynomial.delta (definitions without simp equation lemmas)
findings.excerpt:
| .add p q => eval X p + eval X q
  | .mul p q => eval X p * eval X q
findings.problem: The file defines the interpretation `eval` and the derivation `delta` by structural recursion but gives no simp interface for them. No `@[simp]` equation lemmas such as `eval_add`, `eval_mul`, `eval_gen`, `eval_scalar`, `delta_add`, `delta_mul`, `delta_gen` or `delta_scalar` are provided. Clients therefore name the raw definitions in each `simp`/`simp only` call. For example, TraceCocycle.lean repeats `simp only [delta, eval, hp, hq, map_add]`, `simp only [eval, map_add, hp, hq]` and `simp only [eval, map_mul, hp, hq]` in `eval_delta_encoded` and `map_eval`. Inside this file, `eval_delta`, `hasDerivAt_eval` and `norm_eval` rewrite the same four constructor cases by hand. Unfolding by name is more fragile than a stable lemma set, because it depends on the definitions being structurally recursive and unfoldable by the equation compiler. It also makes it impossible to simp `eval` and `delta` of a compound `Expr` without exposing the definition.
findings.proposed_change: Right after the definitions, add the constructor equation lemmas for `eval` and `delta`, for example `@[simp] theorem eval_add (X : ι → A) (p q : Expr ι) : eval X (.add p q) = eval X p + eval X q := rfl`, and the analogous `eval_mul`, `eval_gen`, `eval_scalar` (`= algebraMap ℂ A c`), `delta_add`, `delta_mul`, `delta_gen` and `delta_scalar` (`= .scalar 0`). Do the same for `degree` and `mass` if the unfolding there should also be controlled. Then downstream `simp [wordExpr, eval]` and `simp only [delta, eval, ...]` calls can use `simp [eval_add, eval_mul, ...]` or plain `simp`, and the definitions stay folded. Keep `Expr` reduction in the normal form `eval X (.add p q) = eval X p + eval X q`, which is terminating because the argument shrinks structurally.
findings.benefit: Callers get a named, terminating simp set that pushes `eval` and `delta` through `+` and `*` without unfolding the definitions. The repeated four-case inductions in TraceCocycle.lean (`eval_delta_encoded`, `map_eval`) and in this file become shorter and less sensitive to how the definitions are implemented.
